author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A passenger train derailed between Rouen and Caen in northern France on Friday evening, injuring about 20 people, French authorities said. The incident occurred near Cleon in Normandy at about 7:54 p.m. local time.

French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said 180 passengers were aboard the train. About 140 firefighters were sent to the scene to assist injured passengers and help others leave the train. The prefecture of Seine-Maritime asked the public to avoid the area while emergency crews worked.

Authorities had not immediately released details on the severity of the injuries or the cause of the derailment. Rail service on the corridor was expected to face disruption during the response and investigation. The situation remained developing Friday as emergency teams accounted for passengers and secured the site. Travelers in the region should rely on official rail and local-authority updates before beginning a trip, because early casualty and service information can change as responders complete their work.
dek: Authorities said 180 passengers were aboard the train near Cleon, where 140 firefighters responded Friday evening.
headline: Train derailment in northern France injures about 20
